searchText: Looks like the rushed merge is beginning to show its cracks. Thankfully it wasn’t too rushed so the network is resilient. I have not heard/seen anything about the issue other than than "something is wrong". Not sure why it wasn't linked or discussed here [0], but yesterday (before the _second_ wave) these were published: https://twitter.com/potuz1/status/1657031082749861891 https://twitter.com/terencechain/status/1657021042110631936 [0] I mean now that fixes are out, I understand keeping vulnerabilities private until resolved. Call me paranoid, but that might also be the reason why there was a _second_ wave, because who can resist spamming the network with attestations for old targets after those tweets 😉 A few hours ago Teku and Prysm had releases ( https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/releases/tag/v4.0.3-hotfix / https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/releases/tag/23.5.0) which contain the same "old attestation filtering". Doesn't look like this, it is starting to look like normal behavior for some clients if the EL is not responding for a while. This may well be a fairly sized node that is offline pruning or similar. Would be great if someone made a write-up similar to https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/blob/master/docs/postmortems/2021-08-22-split-postmortem.md This issue seems to have occurred because of how overcomplicated Ethereum got post-merge, which is what I warned about 🙂 > Todays incident has been a great firedrill. It looks like two or three issues came together 🙂 Hello, any way to get ahold of at least 1 sepoliaETH for dev purposes?
